relationships.subject: dorsal horn PV+ inhibitory interneurons
relationships.evidence_quote: This increased firing is consistent with a decrease in PV-mediated inhibition, since PV+ interneurons, which show reduced evoked firing following nerve injury (Figure 4F), form synapses onto at least some CCK+ interneurons.

key_findings: Nerve injury does not increase overall dorsal horn reactivity but markedly decorrelates millisecond-scale touch-evoked firing, most strongly in the superficial dorsal horn.

Silencing dorsal horn PV+ interneurons recapitulates this temporal decorrelation and produces allodynia, whereas disrupting GABA-A-dependent presynaptic inhibition or Rorbeta-mediated feed-forward inhibition increases correlated activity instead.
